slides.title: ForeTac-VLA: A Forecasting-Based Tactile-Vision-Language-Action Model for Contact-Rich Robotic Manipulation
slides.highlight: ForeTac-VLA predicts future tactile states to guide action generation in contact-rich environments, contributing to HyECHO's goal of multimodal perception.

card.one_liner: ForeTac-VLA improves contact-rich robotic manipulation by forecasting future tactile states to guide action generation.
card.key_idea: Integrates bidirectional cross-attention for vision-language-tactile fusion and a transformer-based module to predict multi-step future tactile states, conditioned via a ground-truth-to-prediction training curriculum.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on four real-world tasks (e.g., peg insertion) with 20 trials each; achieved 95% average success, significantly outperforming VLA and TacVLA baselines.
card.limitation: Evaluated using only one robot embodiment and tactile sensor configuration with predefined temporal offsets for forecasting.

slides.title: DexTouch-WM: Learning Action-Conditioned Tactile World Models from Human Touch for Dexterous Robot Manipulation
slides.highlight: DexTouch-WM leverages scalable human touch data to predict future RGB observations and bilateral tactile dynamics for dexterous robot manipulation. The model demonstrates that human interaction can serve as a complementary data axis to improve robot-domain visual and contact predictions.

card.one_liner: DexTouch-WM scales robot dexterous manipulation world models using human touch data via shared sensing interfaces.
card.key_idea: An action-conditioned model coupling a video expert with a tactile expert using anatomy-aware tokenization, residual tactile latents, and retargeted human-to-robot action alignment.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on 100h human and 5h robot data; showed improved visual/contact prediction and served as a policy evaluator and synthetic data generator.
card.limitation: Synthetic trajectories for policy training showed inconsistent utility, with some policies performing worse than those trained on all-real data.

slides.title: AVT-Fabric: Active Visuo-Tactile Perception via Adaptive Evidence Selection for Efficient Robotic Fabric Comparison
slides.tldr: ADAPTIVE VISUO-TACTILE PERCEPTION FOR ROBOTIC FABRIC COMPARISON
slides.highlight: This work introduces an RGB-first framework that adaptively selects tactile evidence to improve reasoning accuracy and efficiency. It is relevant to HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception by demonstrating adaptive evidence selection for complex material observation.

card.one_liner: AVT-Fabric adaptively selects tactile evidence to improve robotic fabric comparison accuracy and inference efficiency.
card.key_idea: An RGB-first MLLM framework using a dual-scale gate (confidence and logit margin) to decide whether to process additional force-tagged GelSight observations, utilizing textual memory and majority voting.
card.evaluation: Tested on 400 held-out comparisons and real-robot scenarios; achieved 98.0% accuracy, reducing model-side latency by 61.8% compared to passive inference.
card.limitation: Physical observations are acquired before inference; the system does not yet perform online closed-loop control of contact force or location.

slides.title: Agile-WAM: An Agile Tactile World Action Model for Contact-Rich Robot Control
slides.tldr: AGILE TACTILE WORLD ACTION MODEL FOR CONTACT-RICH CONTROL
slides.highlight: This work introduces a multimodal world action model that jointly predicts future visual and tactile states to improve robot control. It is relevant to HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception and state modeling by demonstrating efficient integration of diverse sensory signals with different timescales.

card.one_liner: Agile-WAM is an efficient tactile world action model for high-frequency, contact-rich robot manipulation.
card.key_idea: Uses a vision-tactile-to-action flow-matching backbone with multi-horizon multimodal prediction, supervising visual latents at longer offsets and tactile latents at shorter offsets to match their distinct timescales.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on 9 simulated and 5 real-world tasks; outperformed baselines in success rate with 11.9ms real-world latency. Results appear trustworthy via extensive ablations.

slides.title: XRoboToolKit-T: Teleoperation with High Stability and Precision with Tactile Sensing for Contact-rich Manipulation
slides.highlight: This work introduces a teleoperation system using a tactile-informed force control architecture to improve stability and precision in contact-rich tasks. It utilizes haptic modules and a vision-language-action model to refine manipulation actions based on real-time tactile sensing.

card.one_liner: XRoboToolKit-T is a tactile-driven teleoperation system enhancing stability and precision for contact-rich robotic manipulation.
card.key_idea: Combines a real-time stabilizer estimating pseudo shear forces to suppress aggressive movements and a VLA-based refiner for task-specific corrective action adjustments using tactile images.
card.evaluation: Tested on syringe insertion and pipette tasks using UR5 arms; outperformed Twist2 in grasping efficiency and improved control frequency to 96.4 Hz.

slides.title: ZeroTouch: Tactile-Supervised Visual Contact Estimation for Contact-Rich Manipulation
slides.highlight: ZeroTouch uses tactile measurements as privileged supervision during training to predict contact deformation and forces from RGB observations, enabling high success rates in contact-rich manipulation without tactile hardware at deployment.

card.one_liner: ZeroTouch predicts contact deformation and 6D wrenches from vision and proprioception without deployment-time tactile sensors.
card.key_idea: A tactile-supervised framework using DINOv2, FiLM, and cross-attention to jointly estimate dense contact deformation, instantaneous 6D wrenches, and grasp-dependent desired compression targets from RGB and robot state.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on 270 grasp episodes and physical trials. Outperformed OpenVLA and SmolVLA, achieving up to 95% success on unseen objects.
card.limitation: Struggles with visually ambiguous physical properties (e.g., internal load shifts) and shows reduced accuracy for certain wrench moment components.

slides.title: PSR: Predictive Sensorimotor Representation Learning for Contact-Rich Manipulation
slides.tldr: PREDICTIVE SENSORIMOTOR REPRESENTATION FOR CONTACT-RICH MANIPULATION
slides.highlight: This work introduces a framework for learning predictive representations from multimodal sensorimotor signals to improve force-aware manipulation. It is relevant to HyECHO's focus on multimodal perception and the integration of diverse sensory signals for state estimation.

card.one_liner: PSR-VLA improves contact-rich manipulation by predicting future sensorimotor dynamics to guide high-precision robotic actions.
card.key_idea: A multimodal Transformer learns a hierarchy of predictive representations (F/T sequences, joint-effort, and state displacement) and integrates them into a VLA policy via gated cross-attention.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on six real-world tasks; PSR-VLA achieved 91.7% success, significantly outperforming $\pi_{0.5}$ and ForceVLA baselines across hard, medium, and easy tasks.
card.limitation: Limited visibility of plug-socket relative pose may hinder initial visual alignment in certain tasks.

slides.title: CommitFlow: Semantic Commitment Verification and Local Correction for Long-Horizon Robot Manipulation VLA Execution
slides.tldr: CLOSED-LOOP EXECUTION FRAMEWORK FOR LONG-HORIZON VLA POLICIES
slides.highlight: CommitFlow improves long-horizon robot manipulation by monitoring semantic commitments and applying local corrections to prevent error propagation without retraining the base policy.

card.one_liner: CommitFlow improves long-horizon VLA execution by verifying physical conditions and applying local corrections before stage transitions.
card.key_idea: A closed-loop framework using a Semantic Commitment Monitor to gate actions, BoundaryFlow for base-action-conditioned residuals, and Relation and Gain Calibration to scale correction strength.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on 11 RoboTwin 2.0 tasks and real-world experiments; achieved 75.9% mean success rate, outperforming base policy π0.5 by 22.7%.
card.limitation: Dependent on RGB-D perception accuracy and predefined task-specific event/precondition templates, limiting extension to open-ended tasks.
